chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Playing house rent parties
summary: Before playing with bands, Thompson learned piano at house rent parties, hired to play all night for small sums.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I had only played for parties, school parties and little parties that people gave at their houses, which were later on recognized as house rent parties. And I'd like to talk a little bit about that.
Yes, I think that would be interesting.
Yes. You've heard of house rent parties, haven't you?
Yes, I have.
You've heard these other piano players, I guess, some of the piano players.
Yes.
Haven't you heard some of them?
Yes, yes.
Can you relate to any of that?
Duke Ellington used to refer to James P.
playing house rent parties in New York City, you know.
Yes, uh-huh.
And also Willie the Lion Smith.
You're talking about James P. Johnson.
Yes.
Right.
Well, that's the type of party you mean.

That's exactly right, in other words these people that you're talking about just happened to have been the giants of the -- of barrel house piano, whatever you want to call it, two hand piano as they called it, or stride piano. But all I know is that these house rent parties were common for guys like me, or pianists who could play the popular music of the day. That's all it was. In other words the people didn't have enough money to hire an orchestra, and usually the house would be too small for that type of orchestra any way.

And so they hired piano players because we could play with enough rhythm, with the use of two hands, and the pat of the foot and the clapping of the hands, you know, and the influence of the alcoholic beverages to keep things moving and swinging, you see.
Yes.
And this is how I really learned how to play the piano, before I even started playing with other

musician, except my own musicians who I tried to get together. But hardly any of the younger musicians had the experience and knowledge how to play. So usually I'd wind up playing by myself and I'd get paid small sums to play for these parties.
Would you play for long lengths of time, or did they let you sit back a little bit, or how much playing did you do at those parties?

At those parties I was hired specifically to play all night, and of course naturally, you know, you'll take an intermission and have some sort of drink of some type, whether you would drink alcohol or whatever, coca cola or whatever. But that was my job, you know, I was hired to play the music, you know. And in those days, of course, one of the most popular types of music for pianists was boogie-woogie.
